readerTitle: Two coffee chains, same profit, different price
caseNote: 가상 사례 (지역 슈퍼마켓 그룹의 전략팀, 12개 매장 커피 체인, 커피 체인 창업자) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 가치 배수는 답이 아니라 요약이다. 같은 이익이라도 남는 현금, 성장, 위험이 다르면 같은 배수를 쓸 수 없다.
misconception: 비슷한 회사가 이익의 10배에 팔렸으니 우리도 이익에 10을 곱하면 된다.

sources.text: 기업 가치평가의 표준 개념 (가치 배수, 가치 동인: 현금 창출, 성장, 위험, 재투자)

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 판매자 제시가: 연 이익 $600,000 × 10 = $6,000,000.
실제 업계 배수 수치는 쓰지 않았습니다. '10배'는 판매자가 주장하는 가상의 비교 거래입니다.

cards.title: Two coffee chains, same profit, different price
body: You work on the strategy team at a regional supermarket group. Your boss wants coffee bars near the stores and has found a 12-shop coffee chain for sale.
The owner has a simple pitch: "We make $600,000 a year. A rival chain just sold for 10 times profit. So we're worth $6 million." Your boss gives you two weeks to say whether that's fair.

image.label: A small coffee shop with a price tag hanging from its awning
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 커피숍 건물 차양에 커다란 가격표가 매달려 있고 "$6M?"라고 적혀 있음. 옆에서 정장 차림 직원이 돋보기로 가격표를 들여다봄. 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표 없음.

cards.title: Is "10 times profit" a fair price?
body: The rival sale is real, and the $600,000 profit checks out in the accounts. What's your first move?

options.text: Accept $6 million. The profit is real and the rival set the price
options.feedback: Fast and easy to defend. But a **valuation multiple** only carries over if the two businesses match on growth, risk and cash needs. You haven't checked yet.

options.text: Check how this chain differs from the rival before using its multiple
options.feedback: This treats the multiple as a starting point, not an answer. The work is finding what made the rival worth 10 times, and whether this chain has it too.

options.text: Ignore the rival and value it on revenue instead
options.feedback: A second view is useful. But revenue hides even more than profit does: two chains with the same sales can keep very different amounts.

cards.title: What the $600,000 really is.
body: Two findings from the accounts. The espresso machines and shop interiors wear out, and keeping them up costs about $150,000 a year. And three shops, all with leases ending within two years, earn half the profit.

cards.title: A multiple is a summary of the drivers.
body: A **valuation multiple** is shorthand. When a buyer pays 10 times profit, they are betting on things behind the profit: how much cash it leaves, how fast it grows and how likely it is to last.
Those are the **drivers of value**. If the rival needed little upkeep and had long leases, its 10 times bought more than this chain's 10 times would. Same profit, less cash, more risk.

image.label: A multiple shown as a lid over three jars: cash, growth, risk
image.brief: 인포그래픽. "10x"라고 적힌 뚜껑 아래 병 세 개: "Cash left", "Growth", "Risk". 판매자 체인 쪽은 Cash 병이 덜 차 있고 Risk 병이 더 차 있음. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Which finding should move the price most?
body: Your notes list three more things. Which one deserves the biggest change to your offer?

options.text: Its latte prices are below rivals', so there's room to raise them
options.feedback: Real upside, and a driver of value. But it's a maybe that you would have to deliver, so you shouldn't pay the seller in full for it.

options.text: The three top shops could lose their leases within two years
options.feedback: This hits the **risk** driver hardest. Half the profit could vanish or cost far more in rent, so this deserves the biggest discount or a deal term that protects you.

options.text: Profit fell 5% last year during an unusually rainy summer
options.feedback: A one-off dip tells you little about future cash. Overweighting it gives you a lower offer but no better picture of the business.

cards.title: Your number is a range, not a fact.
body: The analysis points below $6 million, maybe nearer $4.5 million before the lease risk. But small changes in your guesses about rent or growth move the answer a lot. Present a range and say what would move it.
Also, the right price for you isn't only what the chain is worth on paper. If another buyer values it more, a low offer simply loses the deal. Decide your walk-away number before you negotiate.

cards.title: Now you're the coffee chain's founder.
body: You own a similar chain and plan to sell in about a year. You have time and money for one big move to raise what buyers will pay. Which one?

options.text: Open three new shops fast to show growth
options.feedback: Growth is a driver of value, but new shops cost cash and haven't proven themselves yet. Buyers may count them as risk, not profit.

options.text: Lock in longer leases on your best shops
options.feedback: This lowers the **risk** behind your profit, so a buyer can justify a higher **multiple** on the same earnings. Nothing about the coffee changes.

options.text: Delay machine repairs to make this year's profit look higher
options.feedback: Profit rises on paper, but careful buyers check upkeep. They'll subtract the overdue repairs and trust your other numbers less.

cards.title: Before you multiply, check what the multiple is buying.
body: Two ideas did the work here:
list: **Valuation multiples:** a quick price, but only fair if the businesses match
**What drives value:** cash left after upkeep, growth, and how long the profit will last
cards.callout: **Try it today:** take your own business's yearly profit. Subtract the spending you need each year just to keep it running. Then list the one thing that could make that profit disappear.
cards.softwareNote: For a software company, the same check applies: subtract the engineering needed just to keep the product working, and ask how much revenue depends on a few large customers.
